subject: Career
title: Maslach's Three Dimensions of Burnout
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Maslach's Three Dimensions of Burnout.

hook.text: Exhaustion alone isn't burnout. Christina Maslach discovered it's a triple threat that erodes you from three directions.

buildup.text: The Maslach Burnout Inventory measures three dimensions: emotional exhaustion, depersonalization, and reduced accomplishment.

discovery.text: Exhaustion = drained. Depersonalization = cynical detachment. Reduced accomplishment = feeling ineffective despite effort.

twist.text: You can be exhausted but not burned out. True burnout requires all three. That's why vacations alone don't fix it.

climax.text: Maslach's framework helps you identify which dimension is affected most — and target your recovery.

punchline.text: Burnout has three faces. Treat the right one.

quiz.question: What are Maslach's three dimensions of burnout?
options: Emotional exhaustion, depersonalization, and reduced accomplishment

details.summary: Christina Maslach's model defines burnout through three dimensions: emotional exhaustion (feeling drained), depersonalization (cynicism toward work and people), and reduced personal accomplishment (feeling ineffective). These dimensions can manifest independently or together.
details.whyItMatters: Maslach's model is the most validated framework in burnout research. It enables precise measurement through the Maslach Burnout Inventory, guiding millions of clinical assessments worldwide.
takeaways: Emotional exhaustion is the most commonly reported burnout dimension
Depersonalization creates distance between a person and their work
Reduced accomplishment erodes self-confidence and motivation

faq.question: Do all three dimensions of burnout appear simultaneously?
faq.answer: Not necessarily. Emotional exhaustion typically appears first, followed by depersonalization as a coping mechanism. Reduced personal accomplishment may develop independently or as a consequence of the other two. Different individuals show different patterns.

faq.question: How is the Maslach Burnout Inventory used in practice?
faq.answer: The MBI is a standardized questionnaire with 22 items measuring all three dimensions. Organizations use it for workforce assessments, researchers use it in clinical studies, and therapists use it to track patient progress. Scores on each dimension are evaluated independently.
